hero.title: Hi, I'm Mateusz
hero.lead: I'm a Computer Science student at Cracow University of Technology, constantly growing my programming skills while working at Shelfio.

paragraphs: Outside of studying and work, physical activity is what gives me a lot of joy. Most often that means the gym and running, which teach me consistency and give me a break from a sedentary lifestyle.

My passions are diving and travelling. I hold an OWD certificate and dive recreationally during the season - I love exploring underwater spaces and discovering new places on the map. It lets me combine a taste for adventure with the need to get to know the world. My dream is to see and experience as much as I can.

I simply enjoy trying new things and seeing where they take me. After hours I build mobile apps in React Native, and lately I've been drawn into electronics - Arduino, ESP32 and my own small circuits.

projects.title: My projects
projects.lead:
Today mostly React and React Native. Earlier C and C++ -
 systems programming and algorithms.

descriptions.philo: A simulation of the dining philosophers problem: threads, mutexes and semaphores with no deadlocks or race conditions.
descriptions.minishell: A two-person team project: a Bash-style shell - parser, pipes, redirections, environment variables and builtin commands.
descriptions.gymbox: Landing page for GymBox - a showcase site for a gym, deployed at gymbox.pl.
descriptions.warehouse: A mobile warehouse management app: React Native with Expo on the front end, Ruby on Rails as the backend.
descriptions.pushswap: Sorting stacks in the smallest possible number of operations - complexity analysis and optimisation.
descriptions.portfolio: This very site - built in Next.js, taken from Figma all the way to deployment.

items.description: Theoretical foundation: algorithms and data structures, discrete mathematics, databases, computer networks.
I develop frontend and backend features in a production application: JavaScript and TypeScript, React, Ruby on Rails and tests. Teamwork, code review and production deployments.
Peer-to-peer model, no lecturers. Projects in C and C++, peer code review and teamwork under deadline pressure.
I taught Python to children and teenagers - online classes, my own materials and regular contact with parents.
